label: Came meleon (chamaeleon thistle)
summary: The rubricated plant name of this entry: the chamaeleon thistle of the Dioscoridean tradition.
canonical: chamaeleon (Dioscorides; identification disputed between Atractylis gummifera L. and Cardopatium corymbosum (L.) Pers.)

label: capomilla (camomile)
summary: Camomile, whose oil carries the eye ointment at the close of the usage paragraph.

label: aloes
summary: Aloes, the bitter purgative resin that opens the later-hand pill recipe.
canonical: aloes (drug of Aloe spp., probably Aloe vera (L.) Burm.f. or A. perryi Baker)

label: mirabolani (myrobalans)
summary: Myrobalans, the imported purgative fruits, here unspecified as to kind.
canonical: myrobalans (dried fruits of Terminalia and Phyllanthus spp., unspecified kind)

label: mastice (mastic)
summary: Mastic resin, a stomachic binder in the pill recipe.

label: dragaganti (tragacanth?)
summary: Probably gum tragacanth; the reading of the word itself is provisional.
canonical: unresolved - probably gum tragacanth (Astragalus spp.), but the word is only provisionally read

label: rose rubee (red roses)
summary: Red roses, the astringent corrective of the pill mass.
canonical: red roses (Rosa gallica L. of the apothecaries, not certain from the page)

label: croco (saffron)
summary: Saffron, listed with its quantity partly illegible.

label: asaro (asarum?)
summary: A provisionally read ingredient, perhaps asarum.
canonical: unresolved - perhaps asarum (Asarum europaeum L.), perhaps another word entirely
